designedAgainst.note: Design only. No runtime module imports this file; nothing here is available to a learner. Product availability stays false until a dedicated C1 release gate.

assumedPriorLevelCapabilities.description: give an opinion and back it with at least one reason
build a short argument with a claim and support, in a familiar-topic conversation
compare two options and state which is better and why
explain a position that has more than one part
reach a simple agreement with another party
choose formal/informal language on purpose for a known situation
keep a conversation going without a script, including some repair
summarize a short text's main point for someone who has not read it

canDo: take and defend a position on an abstract or complex topic, qualify it precisely, and concede a fair counterpoint without abandoning it
choose and adjust register on purpose for the audience, and mid-conversation when the situation shifts, and notice and repair their own register slips
take in a longer or more complex message and relay it accurately and usefully to someone who does not have the original
infer meaning that is not stated directly and mark their own claims with an honest degree of certainty
produce an extended, organized turn with a beginning, a development and a close, and self-correct mid-turn without losing the thread

negotiate toward a mutually acceptable outcome when constraints genuinely conflict, ask a precisely targeted question when an instruction is ambiguous, and propose and defend an alternative when the first plan does not work
sustain a conversation across two or three related topic shifts, refer back to something said earlier, and close a longer interaction with a short accurate summary
cannotYet: claim complete CEFR C1 mastery: listening, speaking and pronunciation remain out of scope
handle dense literary, academic-citation or highly idiomatic/poetic register
participate in live/professional interpretation or specialized legal/medical register
negotiate with more than two parties at once
reliably recognize irony/understatement outside the explicitly taught patterns
write essay-length formal text with citation conventions
definition.interactionCeiling: two-to-three related topics per conversation, extended multi-sentence turns permitted, register may shift mid-conversation, repair available and support fading as evidence allows

vocabularyBudget.note: Budget ceilings for LC-CONT-C1, not a pre-committed catalogue. Counts are weighted toward hedging/certainty/register vocabulary and argumentation/negotiation vocabulary, per c1.md section 6.

reuseMatrix.invariant: every required capability's row has at least one non-null mark in an arc after its introduction arc, EXCEPT the three required capabilities introduced in the level's own final arc (sustain_a_conversation_across_topic_shifts, refer_back_to_earlier_discourse, shift_register_within_one_conversation), which have no later arc to reuse in. Their evidence path instead comes from multiple episodes within sustained_interaction itself, the same one-arc evidence pattern the live A1 blueprint uses for introduce_someone_else (arc 3, three episodes, independent target reached inside the arc). Their further reuse becomes a cross-level input for a future C2 blueprint, not an unmet requirement of this one.

evidence.note: independent=3 for required capabilities is higher than A1's independent=2 because C1 evidence includes a pragmatic/register dimension not reliably established by one or two successes; see c1.md section 9.

evaluationIntents.intentReuse: repair_request with a new repairKind subtype: ask_for_precision

cefrCitationCaveat: Scale names referenced above (Sociolinguistic Appropriateness, Coherence and Cohesion, Overall Oral/Written Production, Sustained Monologue, Conversation, Formal Discussion and Meetings, Goal-oriented Co-operation, Processing Text / Mediating a Text, Reading for Information and Argument) are real CEFR Companion Volume (2020) scale titles used as reference points, not verbatim descriptor quotations. Verification against the primary CEFR Companion Volume text is an open item for LC-AUD-001 or a later dedicated pass.

fourStrandsAudit.readingListeningCeiling: only reading-based meaning-focused input is implemented and tested; no listening comprehension claim is made

explicitExclusions: listening comprehension, speaking, pronunciation or any live/voice interaction
dense literary or highly idiomatic/poetic language, academic citation conventions, professional legal/medical register
multi-party (3+ simultaneous interlocutors) negotiation or discussion
essay-length formal writing with citation/structure conventions
generalized humor/wordplay recognition beyond the explicitly taught understatement/irony patterns
any claim of complete CEFR C1 certification

coreEngineRequirements.problem: existing evaluation primarily judges intent/pattern match; C1 needs a response marked wrong or partially credited for wrong register even when intent and grammar are correct
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: no register_appropriateness scoring dimension is documented in the existing evaluation model
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: hybrid evaluator gains a register-appropriateness signal scored independently of intent-match correctness
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: low if the new dimension defaults to not-scored below C1
coreEngineRequirements.testsRequired: register-mismatch fixtures per intent; confirm lower levels unaffected

coreEngineRequirements.problem: use_cohesive_devices_across_a_turn and track_discourse need to evaluate whether several sentences in one turn cohere, not just whether each sentence individually passes
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: an evaluator path that accepts a multi-sentence turn and returns an overall coherence signal plus per-capability credit
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: moderate: touches shared evaluator plumbing; must not change scoring for existing single-utterance step types
coreEngineRequirements.testsRequired: coherent vs flat-list vs contradictory multi-sentence fixtures

coreEngineRequirements.problem: crediting an accurate reference to something said several turns earlier requires the runtime to retain and check against that earlier turn's content
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: not documented in existing session/planner behaviour; closest analog is a fixed-script roleplay, not a dynamically referenced history
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: a bounded conversation-history buffer the evaluator can check a later turn's reference against, scoped to a single session/episode run
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: low if additive and opt-in per episode
coreEngineRequirements.testsRequired: correct-reference, vague-reference and misattributed-reference fixtures against a scripted conversation history

coreEngineRequirements.problem: personalizing 'the negotiated good/service' does not cleanly fit existing semantic types (object, place, activity, topic, subject)
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: no slot type for a personalizable transactional item/service with a neutral fallback
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: a new semantic type with the same neutral-fallback contract as existing personalizable slots
coreEngineRequirements.testsRequired: personalization-invariant tests per the two-theme proof requirement
coreEngineRequirements.note: check whether a sibling A2/B1/B2 blueprint already requested an equivalent type before building this twice

qaAcceptance.note: Acceptance target for LC-CONT-C1; not yet met since C1 has no runtime episodes.
items: curriculum authoring contract equivalent for C1 episodes
at least 20 varied learner-shaped journeys per completed arc
two consecutive full clean cycles after the final fix

crossLevelAcceptance.note: Cannot be satisfied by this blueprint alone; this is what LC-AUD-001 must verify once A2/B1/B2 blueprints exist.
openItems: confirm every assumed prior-level capability in assumedPriorLevelCapabilities actually exists in the merged B1/B2 blueprints
confirm B2's actual exit vocabulary/pattern ceiling is compatible with abstract_argument's entry assumptions

confirm none of C1's 28 capabilities semantically duplicates an A2/B1/B2 capability under a different name, particularly weigh_implications_of_a_position vs the assumed B2 advantages/disadvantages capability
confirm cross-level reuse of B1/B2 capabilities inside C1 arcs, not just within-C1 reuse
independently audit the complexity-rise claim in c1.md section 17 against the real B2 blueprint

humanPilotQuestions: does an abstract-topic argument feel meaningfully harder than a B2 familiar-topic argument, or does the jump feel arbitrary?
do learners perceive register feedback as useful correction or as unwelcome social judgment?
does inferring implied meaning feel like a legitimate skill or like guessing what the app wants to hear?
does the negotiation arc's mid-conversation complication feel like a fair complexity increase or like the app moving the goalposts?
does the sustained-interaction arc's personalized topic-shift content feel personally relevant or contrived?
delayed retention: do learners who pass a capability's independent target in its home arc still produce it correctly, unprompted, in sustained_interaction weeks later?
does the independent=3 threshold feel appropriately rigorous or needlessly repetitive compared to A1's independent=2?
